football_evidence.question: Can Illinois’ pass rush get to Oregon’s quarterback?
football_evidence.assessment: No material disagreement: EdgeDesk and the line are within 1.3 points.
supporting: When Oregon has the ball (big plays on the ground): Oregon’s offense turns 3.0% of its runs into explosive gains, and Illinois’ defense gives up explosive gains on 3.5% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When Illinois has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Illinois’ offense is stopped at or behind the line on 10.8% of its runs, and Oregon’s defense stops 18.3% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.3%).
When Oregon has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Oregon’s offense averages 4.1 yards per carry, and Illinois’ defense allows 4.3 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).
In his last two games (UCLA and Nebraska), Raiola averaged 2.8 yards per attempt, against 11.2 in his two games before that.
contradicting: When Oregon has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Oregon’s offense has allowed a sack on 3.1% of its dropbacks, and Illinois’ defense sacks the quarterback on 2.7% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
In his last two games (Purdue and Michigan State), Houser averaged 6.3 yards per attempt, against 8.5 in his four games before that.
Dante Moore has completed 70 of 100 passes (70.0%) for 935 yards, 9.4 yards per attempt, 9 touchdowns and no interceptions in four games for Oregon, and has been sacked on 6 of 106 dropbacks.
In his last two games (portlandstate and USC), Moore averaged 10.8 yards per attempt, against 8.6 in his two games before that.
